question.:question/problem: Find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}$ when $f(x)=(2 x - 6)^{4}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=g^{4},\,g=2 x - 6
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=4g^{3},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =4g^{3}\cdot (2) \\  & =8(2 x - 6)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given that $f(x)=(x^{2} - 5 x + 1)^{3},$ the slope at the point $(1,-27)$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule to find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}.$

First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=g^{3},\,g=x^{2} - 5 x + 1
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=3g^{2},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=2 x - 5.
$$

Multiplying the two together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =3g^{2}\cdot (2 x - 5) \\  & =3(x^{2} - 5 x + 1)^{2}(2 x - 5).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line at the point where $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|_{x=1} & =[3(x^{2} - 5 x + 1)^{2}(2 x - 5)]|_{x=1} \\  & =3((1)^{2} - 5 (1) + 1)^{2}(2 (1) - 5) \\  & =3(-3)^{2}(-3) \\  & =-81.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, let's define a function $h(t):$

$$
h(t)=(- 2 t^{2} - 5)^{3}
$$

To differentiate this function, we use the chain rule. Let 

$$
g(t)=- 2 t^{2} - 5,\,h(g(t))=g(t)^{3}.
$$

Differentiating our functions, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}g^{′}(t) & =(- 2 t^{2} - 5)^{′}=- 4 t, \\ h^{′}(g(t)) = (g^{3})^{′}=3g^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[(- 2 t^{2} - 5)^{3}] & =h^{′}(t) \\  & =h^{′}(g(t))\cdot g^{′}(t) \\  & =3g^{2}\cdot - 4 t \\  & =3(- 2 t^{2} - 5)^{2}(- 4 t).\end{aligned}
$$
